corrected_value.title: Temporary suppression of visual processing in an RSVP task: An attentional blink?

decisions.quote: In this study, we replicated Experiment 2 from Raymond, Shapiro, and Arnell’s (1992) seminal paper that made the attentional blink phenomenon famous (the phenomenon was first revealed by Broadbent & Broadbent, 1987, and Weichselgartner & Sperling, 1987).
decisions.reason: Both shipped (input_row_index 2163) and blind (target_index 0) identify the same tested original paper: Raymond, Shapiro, and Arnell (1992), 'Temporary suppression of visual processing in an RSVP task: An attentional blink?'. The conflicting_dois pairing flag is solely due to a legacy double slash in the shipped APA DOI (10.1037//0096-1523.18.3.849 vs. 10.1037/0096-1523.18.3.849 in the paper's reference list). Both Experiments 1 and 2 of the present paper re-test Experiment 2 of Raymond et al. (1992), whereas earlier citations (Broadbent & Broadbent, 1987; Weichselgartner & Sperling, 1987) are historical background.

decisions.quote: From a statistical point of view, the results of our experiment largely replicated the specific pattern of results of Raymond et al. (1992), but they also showed some differences. Specifically, the differences concerned the absolute level of performance and a difference in the onset, peak, and offset of the blink that were found one lag earlier in comparison to those observed by Raymond et al. (1992).
decisions.location: Experiment 1, Results, Replication assessment, p. 662 (also Abstract, p. 656; Experiment 2, pp. 663-664; General discussion, pp. 664-666)
decisions.reason: Across both Experiments 1 and 2, the authors explicitly frame their results as partly replicating Raymond et al. (1992) (confirming the attentional blink and its overall magnitude and duration/width) and partly differing in statistically substantial ways (lower overall accuracy of ~75% vs. ~90% in the control condition, onset/peak/offset shifted one lag earlier, reduced lag-1 sparing, and lack of convergence at ceiling at lags 7-8). While surveyed experts emphasized the similarities, the authors contrast the expert ratings with their own statistical comparisons and explicitly state that 'some results provided in the original report were not entirely replicated', matching the codebook definition of 'mixed'.

decisions.quote: We conducted a replication project on an original phenomenon that was discovered more than 25 years ago, namely the attentional blink (Raymond, Shapiro, & Arnell, Human Perception and Performance, 18(3), 849–860, 1992), which has been conceptually replicated hundreds of times with major variations. Here, we ran two identical experiments, adopting the new practices and closely reproducing the original experiment. The two experiments were run by different research groups in different countries and laboratories with different participants.
decisions.reason: The authors collected new empirical data from two independent samples of participants (Experiment 1 in Italy, N = 98 analyzed; Experiment 2 in the UK, N = 29 analyzed) to directly re-test Experiment 2 of Raymond, Shapiro, and Arnell (1992), which makes the record a 'replication'.
